text: **dsh-tool-search** 是 DeepSeek Harness 的工具搜索与精简插件，通过 system-prompt/assemble 按工具目录大小和令牌预算，将长尾工具收纳到分组清单，并保留核心工具及搜索、描述、调用三个桥接工具。用户或项目可配置分组与 rerank 匹配器；搜索在匹配器不可用时退回关键词排序。模型可按需查找工具、读取完整参数并调用真实工具，已发现工具会在会话后续轮次中动态显示。插件还提供配置管理工具、对话式设置技能、可选首轮预加载，以及 PTC/SDK 声明适配，适合工具目录庞大、希望减少每轮上下文开销的 DSH 使用者。

dsh-tool-search trims DSH's visible tool catalog to fit a token budget while keeping core tools ready. The model can search deferred tools by rerank or keywords, load schemas, and invoke tools; discovered tools remain visible in later turns. Groups, preload, and PTC declarations are supported.
我想让 DSH 在工具太多时自动缩短模型看到的清单。
能不能先搜索工具目录，再按需要加载相关工具？
我需要查看某个隐藏工具的参数定义后再决定怎么用。
让模型可以通过工具名和参数调用暂时未展示的工具。
我想用 rerank 模型按用户问题给工具搜索结果排序。
没有配置重排序服务时，工具搜索也能用关键词匹配吗？
我希望搜到或调用过的工具能在后续对话轮次继续显示。
帮我按类别整理工具，并设置全局或项目级的搜索配置。
How can I keep a large DSH tool catalog from filling the model context on every turn?
Can I find and load tools on demand, with keyword search as a fallback when reranking is unavailable?
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「搜索长尾工具」：模型提交查询后，插件用已配置的 rerank 接口排序；没有匹配器或请求失败时改用关键词匹配，并返回工具名称、说明和分组。
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「按预算披露工具」：每轮根据上下文窗口和清单预算，选择完整分组说明、仅名称或分组计数清单；核心工具保持直接可见。
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「加载并调用工具」：模型可读取单个延迟工具的完整参数，或用名称和参数执行真实工具；桥接层返回结果或可见错误信息。
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「会话内动态加载」：搜索、描述或调用后的工具会加入当前会话的可见集合，并按配置的上限淘汰较早加载的工具。
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「对话式配置」：设置技能读取完整工具目录并协助分组，用户确认后可写入用户级或项目级配置，包含匹配器与可选预加载设置。
**dsh-tool-search** 的功能「PTC 工具清单精简」：在严格 PTC 模式保留 `run_code` 传输工具，并重绘 SDK 声明区域，仅列出当前披露的核心与桥接工具。
dsh-tool-search 使用前须知：配置 rerank 匹配器后，搜索查询和候选工具名称、说明会发送到所配置的匹配器端点；未配置时可使用本地关键词匹配（见 src/matcher.ts:34-46）。
dsh-tool-search 提供工具 tool_search：Search the deferred tool catalog and return ranked matches; uses the configured rerank matcher with keyword fallback.
dsh-tool-search 提供工具 tool_describe：Load the full schema of one deferred tool by name.
dsh-tool-search 提供工具 tool_call：Invoke a deferred tool by name with its arguments.
dsh-tool-search 提供工具 tool_slimmer_catalog：List the full tool registry catalog, including visible and deferred tools.
dsh-tool-search 提供工具 tool_slimmer_update_config：Validate and persist groups, rerank matcher, preload, and extra core tools.
dsh-tool-search 提供钩子 system-prompt/assemble：Transform the assembled model-visible tool surface.
dsh-tool-search 提供设置项 enabled：Controls auto, on, or off disclosure mode.

dsh-tool-search README · dsh-tool-search：Tool search & slimming for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness) (DSH): Hermes-style progressive disclosure. When your tool catalog gets large (many MCP servers or plugin tools), every tool's JSON schema is injected into the model context on every turn — wasting tokens on tools the task never uses. This plugin collapses the long tail behind three bridge tools and lets the model discover and load them on demand through a configured **rerank model**.

dsh-tool-search README · dsh-tool-search：- **Core tools stay eager** — file/shell/essential tools are always directly visible.
- **Bridge tools** — `tool_search`, `tool_describe`, `tool_call` replace the deferred schemas.
- **Tiered disclosure** — the visible listing shrinks automatically as the catalog grows.
- **Conversational setup** — the bundled `tool-slimmer-setup` skill groups your tools by talking to you, and guides configuring the rerank model.
- **User or project config** — groups/matcher live in `~/.dsh/dsh-tool-search.json` (global) or `<workspace>/.dsh/dsh-tool-search.json` (per project), your choice.

dsh-tool-search README · Install：```sh
dsh plugin --profile web add dsh-tool-search
```

dsh-tool-search README · How it works：Inspired by [Hermes Agent's Tool Search](https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/docs/user-guide/features/tool-search). On every turn, the plugin's `system-prompt/assemble` listener computes the tier and replaces the model-visible tools:

dsh-tool-search README · How it works：| Tier | Condition | Model sees |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | Small catalog / nothing deferrable | Every tool, bridge absent |
| 1 | Grouped manifest fits the budget | Bridge + `## group` name/description listing |
| 2 | Only names fit | Bridge + names-only listing |
| 3 | Even names overflow | Bridge + one line per group (name: count) |

dsh-tool-search README · How it works：Budget = `min(thresholdPct% × contextWindow, listingMaxTokens)`, recomputed every turn. The manifest rides a runtime context, so it survives complete-prompt composition.

**Dynamic injection**: searching, describing, or calling a deferred tool warms it into the session's visible set (LRU-bounded by `maxWarmTools`), so its full schema is injected into the context for later turns — the model pulls tools into context on demand instead of keeping everything.

dsh-tool-search README · How it works：When `tool_call` runs, the plugin executes the **real tool by name** through `ctx.tools.execute`, so approvals, guards, and session events all reference the underlying tool — never the bridge. `tool_search` ranks with the configured rerank matcher and falls back to keyword matching (exact name > name tokens > description tokens) when no matcher is configured or the rerank call fails.

dsh-tool-search README · Setup (conversational)：Ask your agent:

> 帮我配置 dsh-tool-search 的工具分组

The `tool-slimmer-setup` skill will read the catalog, propose groups, confirm with you, ask whether the config should be **global or per-project**, and guide you through configuring the rerank matcher (required for `tool_search` and preload).

dsh-tool-search README · Configuration：Static tuning lives in your profile `cordis.patch.yml` (restart to change):

```yaml
- id: tool-search
  config:
    enabled: auto        # auto | on | off
    thresholdPct: 5      # listing budget as % of context window

dsh-tool-search README · Configuration：- `groups`: exact tool names and/or name prefixes; a tool belongs to the first matching group.
- `matcher`: an OpenAI-compatible `/v1/rerank` endpoint — the only matcher type. `tool_search` returns setup guidance until one is configured.
- `preload`: optional; when enabled (with a matcher), the session's first turn semantically preloads the top-K matching tools into the eager set.
- The file is watched by mtime and hot-reloads; changes take effect on the next turn.

dsh-tool-search README · Bridge tools：| Tool | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `tool_search(query, limit?)` | Search the deferred catalog (rerank, keyword fallback) and return ranked `{name, description, group}` matches; matches are injected into the visible context |
| `tool_describe(name)` | Load the full schema of one deferred tool; the tool is injected into the visible context |
| `tool_call(name, arguments)` | Invoke a deferred tool by real name; approvals/guards/events use the real tool; the tool is injected into the visible context |

dsh-tool-search README · Design notes & pitfalls：- Slimming only rewrites the **model-visible surface** (`system-prompt/assemble`); the registry stays complete, so deferred tools remain executable.
- The bridge, the two setup tools, and `skill` are always eager and never defer themselves.
- **PTC (`run_code`) scopes keep the transport, not the declarations.** Such a scope's wire table is collapsed to `run_code` alone, with every declaration moved into the `tools:sdk` prompt section — the tokens this plugin exists to slim. The plugin leaves that table alone (replacing it deleted `run_code` from the prompt) and re-renders the section instead: the eager core plus the bridge tools, with the deferred catalog injected as a runtime context under a `run_code`-aware header. The section's generator is read from its own text (`interface ToolArgsMap` = TypeScript, `TypedDict` = Python); text from an unknown generator is left untouched rather than rewritten in the wrong language. A `both` scope keeps `run_code` eager (the bridge refuses to invoke it by name) and gets the same declaration rewrite; native sessions are unaffected.
